paragraphs.text: Hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is an autosomal recessive disorder. It is characterized by reduced plasma sulfate and increased urinary sulfate excretion, together with skeletal involvement. The skeletal findings range from short stature and scoliosis to a mild spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (van de Kamp et al., 2023; Tise et al., 2025).

checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance follows from the biallelic variants in the patient and the heterozygous parents.

paragraphs.text: Van de Kamp et al. (2023) reported a Dutch boy whose parents were nonconsanguineous. He presented at 4 months of age with enlarged knees that could not fully extend. His length (-0.5 SDS) and head circumference (+0.5 SDS) were normal. Radiographs showed ovoid vertebral bodies, spiky widening of the metaphyses, irregular tarsal bones, slight flaring of the ribs, and small irregular epiphyses with delayed epiphyseal ossification. The skull and pelvis were normal. Later findings included abnormal gait, a forearm fracture, enlarged elbows, reduced movement of the lumbar spine and knees, winged scapulae, hypermobile fingers, flat feet, and a relatively short trunk. He did not have short stature. Bone mineral density of the proximal femur was reduced (Z-score -2.1), and bone age was advanced. He had autistic features and panic attacks but no intellectual disability, seizures, joint pain, or skin abnormalities. Serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, PTH, and vitamin D were normal. The early spondyloepimetaphyseal abnormalities improved with age. By 11 years, only flattening of the cervical vertebral bodies and irregular lumbar endplates remained. He also had persistent fatigue, chronic cough, recurrent respiratory infections, and elevated sweat chloride. These findings were attributed to another cause.

paragraphs.text: Probands 3 and 4 of Tise et al. (2025) were male and female twins born at 34 weeks' gestation. Proband 3 had onset at 10 months. Skeletal surveys showed exaggerated thoracic kyphosis and lumbar lordosis, and anterior beaking of several thoracic and lumbar vertebral bodies with platyspondyly. They also showed short, broad femoral necks and proximal and distal flaring of the femoral and tibial metaphyses, consistent with spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD), as well as nonossification of the proximal humeral epiphyses. He had S-shaped thoracolumbar scoliosis, pectus carinatum, broad toes, and proportionate stature that was shorter than expected. His past medical history included a type 1 Chiari malformation with resolved ventriculomegaly, a surgically repaired atrial septal defect, idiopathic thrombocytopenia, and strabismus. Urine glycosaminoglycans were normal. His twin sister (proband 4) had skeletal surveys at 14 months and 2 years of age. These showed ovoid vertebral bodies with anterior wedging, broad and short femoral necks, widened metaphyses of the tubular bones, and fragmented proximal epiphyses, consistent with SEMD. She had a normal gait, broad thumbs, 2-3 toe syndactyly, and short, broad halluces. Her height was 134.4 cm (20th percentile, z = -0.85), which was shorter than expected.

paragraphs.text: Tise et al. (2025) identified biallelic SLC13A1 mutations in 5 children from 4 families with HSSD. In proband 1, trio exome sequencing found compound heterozygous mutations: a paternally inherited R12X and a maternally inherited gly448-to-asp (G448D) substitution. In proband 2, a targeted search of SLC13A1 found a homozygous tyr582-to-his (Y582H) mutation with confirmed biparental inheritance. In the affected twins (probands 3 and 4), quad exome sequencing found compound heterozygous mutations: a paternally inherited leu516-to-pro (L516P) substitution and a maternally inherited trp48-to-ter (W48X) mutation. In proband 5, trio genome sequencing found a homozygous W48X mutation with confirmed biparental inheritance. Tise et al. (2025) expressed the missense variants R237C, G448D, L516P, and Y582H in stably transfected MDCK cells. None showed detectable [35S]-sulfate transport, but their plasma membrane localization was similar to wildtype, suggesting that the substitutions affect transport rather than trafficking. They also built a homology model of SLC13A1 based on the SLC13A5 structure. The model predicted that the missense substitutions disrupt contacts and hydrogen bonds or introduce clashes in transmembrane helices TM5, TM9, and TM10 or in the extracellular C terminus.

paragraphs.text: In male and female twins with HSSD and spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (probands 3 and 4), Tise et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygosity for a maternally inherited c.144G-A transition in the SLC13A1 gene (NM_022444.4), resulting in a trp48-to-ter (W48X) substitution, and a paternally inherited L516P mutation. The mutations were found by quad exome sequencing. In an unrelated boy with scoliosis, proportionate short stature, and neurodevelopmental features (proband 5), trio genome sequencing found a homozygous W48X mutation with confirmed biparental inheritance. Van de Kamp et al. (2023) had noted a global allele frequency of 0.05% for this variant.
